temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Small, 5–6 oz (150 g) 375°F / 190°C · 13 min 400°F / 205°C · 17 min Medium, 7–8 oz (220 g) 375°F / 190°C · 16 min 400°F / 205°C · 21 min Large, 10–12 oz (300 g) 375°F / 190°C · 20 min 400°F / 205°C · 27 min Why air-fried chicken breast dries out A chicken breast is a wedge: thick at one end and thin at the other. In the fast-moving air of a basket the thin end reaches 165°F minutes before the thick end, and by the time the centre is safe the tip is dry and stringy. Even the thickness out before cooking. Either pound the thick end under cling film until the whole breast is roughly the same depth, or slice a large breast horizontally into two thinner cutlets. Then take it out as soon as the thickest part reads 165°F, not later. Every extra minute squeezes out juice. Worked example Two medium breasts, about 8 oz each, brushed with oil and seasoned. Preheat for 4 minutes, then cook at 375°F for 16 minutes, turning them at 8 minutes so both sides colour. A larger 12 oz breast needs about 20 minutes at the same temperature. The same breasts would take 21 minutes at 400°F in a conventional oven, so the air fryer saves a few minutes and gives a browner outside. How to tell it is done Use a thermometer in the thickest part, held sideways so the tip sits in the centre rather than poking through. 165°F (74°C) is safe instantly; the reading climbs a few degrees more while it rests. Without a thermometer, cut into the thickest part: the meat should be white all the way through with clear juices, not pink or glassy. Rest the chicken for five minutes on a board before slicing, or the juice ends up on the board instead of in the meat. Before it goes in Pat the breast dry with paper towel so the surface browns instead of steaming, then rub it with a teaspoon of oil and season. A quick brine of 30 minutes in salted water makes a noticeable difference to juiciness. Leave space between breasts in the basket; two that touch steam where they meet. Breaded breasts take the same temperature but a minute or two longer for the coating to set. Related presets Chicken wings 400°F · 22 min · flip at 11 Chicken thighs 380°F · 24 min · flip at 12 Chicken drumsticks 380°F · 22 min · flip at 11 400°F oven to air fryer, every food → Oven to air fryer converter → All food presets → Printable conversion chart → Frequently asked questions How long does chicken breast take in the air fryer? About 16 minutes at 375°F for a medium 7–8 oz breast, turned at 8 minutes. Small breasts take around 13 minutes and large ones around 20. Always finish by temperature, not time. What temperature should chicken breast be when it is done? 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part. Take it out as soon as it reads that; it keeps rising slightly while it rests. Do I need to flip chicken breast in the air fryer? Yes, once, at about the halfway point. The underside gets less direct air and stays paler; turning it gives an even colour on both sides. Can I cook frozen chicken breast in the air fryer? Yes, but it needs a lower temperature and a longer time so the centre is safe before the outside dries. Use frozen mode for frozen chicken rather than this fresh setting. What is the oven equivalent of this air fryer setting? 400°F for about 21 minutes in a conventional oven, or 375°F for 18 minutes in a fan oven.
